Method of Attack: Uses malicious Excel (.xls) attachments with macros that prompt users to 'Enable Content' to run malicious macros; uses fake Windows Defender Antivirus themed document templates to trick users into enabling macros; steals bank credentials, Windows domain credentials, and provides remote access; installs ransomware such as ProLock once network access is gained
Attack Vector: Spam emails with malicious Excel attachments; phishing campaigns using fake invoices, payment and banking information, scanned documents; malware infection via Emotet botnet spam
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious Excel (.xls) attachments; spam emails with Qbot malware; fake Windows Defender Antivirus alert templates; prompt to 'Enable Content' or 'Enable Editing' in Excel; installation of Emotet malware following macro execution
